raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Export idle offload usage and development-operation gauges at startup without
overwriting real multiprocess samples. Related: #59988 and #60001.

## Claims

- Initialize known native/SimpleCPUOffload usage series for every supplied
  engine, and sleep/RL in-flight operation labels during router registration.
- Preserve real SimpleCPUOffload samples during late/concurrent initialization
  and native samples during same-process recorder recreation, including later
  real zero updates.
- Export startup defaults through both `/metrics` and `/metrics/`, without
  duplicate real samples or HTTP counters.

Duplicate-work checks: reread #59988 and searched open PRs for `59988 in:body`,
`gauge startup offload`, and `mostrecent gauge`. #60001 changes scheduler gauges
only; this PR does not change its logger or test. Other results address capacity,
config-info, slot sizing, or Rust metrics, not these Python usage/operation fixes.

## Validation

The following checks were run by the AI assistant after rebasing on 2026-10-18.
Zihao Yang previously confirmed line-by-line review and a personal relevant
test run, and authorized publishing this rebased update.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Offload metrics, reader, histogram suites after rebase | 104 passed |
| RL, sleep and exporter CPU suites after rebase | 40 passed, 20 deselected |
| HTTP status metrics after rebase | 12 passed |
| Pre-rebase startup/recreation compatibility, Prometheus 0.18/0.22/0.25/0.26 | 4 passed per version |
| Pre-rebase cleanup ownership, Prometheus 0.18/0.22/0.25/0.26 | Passed per version |
| Pre-commit (ruff, mypy 3.11, test tethering) / mypy 3.12 wrapper | Passed after rebase |
| Pre-rebase content type, OpenAPI metadata, all/liveall startup and recreation probes | Passed |

On the pre-squash head, upstream pre-commit did not run because the repository's
[contributor-eligibility check](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/38031077208/job/114151970609)
failed (zero merged PRs and no qualifying label). The
[docs build](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35056036/) also stopped
at that gate before building documentation. Local checks above passed; these
upstream statuses are not a claim of successful CI validation.

The late-writer, deterministic concurrent-initialization, native-recreation,
cleanup-ownership, and multiprocess endpoint regressions failed before their
respective fixes and passed afterward. Tests use fresh interpreters with
multiprocess configuration set before Prometheus imports and actual connector
recorders. They cover engines 0 and 3, both mostrecent modes, and real zero updates.
The added tests extend existing suites selected by the CPU KV-connector and
entrypoints/serve Buildkite jobs.

### Serving Validation

These GPU smoke runs predate the 2026-10-18 rebase and were not repeated on the
new upstream base. The post-rebase results above use CPU tests and HTTP clients.

Actual `facebook/opt-125m` weights, revision
`27dcfa74d334bc871f3234de431e71c6eeba5dd6`, RTX 5090, FP16, eager TRITON_ATTN,
512-token context, 64 MiB GPU/CPU caches, Prometheus 0.26.0. One run per row:

| Connector | API workers | Validation revision | Reload counter | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SimpleCPUOffload | 1 | Before cleanup/doc and final native fixes | 7 blocks | Passed; late writer preserved usage 1 |
| SimpleCPUOffload | 2 | Before cleanup/doc and final native fixes | 7 blocks | Passed; late writer preserved usage 1 |
| Native offload | 1 | Before cleanup/doc and final native fixes | 4718592 bytes | Passed |
| Native offload | 2 | Before cleanup/doc and final native fixes | 4718592 bytes | Passed |
| Native offload | 2 | After the final fix | 4718592 bytes | Passed |

Each run checked startup gauges, completions, cache reload, sleep/wake, KV-cache
release, rejected weight-update requests, and final idle-operation counts.
Greedy completions matched before/after cache reset and wake for prompt tokens
`[2] + list(range(100, 227))`, `max_tokens=8`, `temperature=0`, `seed=42`:
`m and I do not know if I`.

This is a serving smoke evaluation, not a broad model-accuracy or performance
benchmark. Full upstream GPU CI, a live elastic-scaling deployment, successful
trainer-driven weight transfer, and a full API-worker restart were not exercised.
The actual recorder reconstruction is covered by the native unit regression.

<details>
<summary>Test commands and serving reproduction</summary>

The post-rebase commands use Python 3.12, Torch 2.11.0, Prometheus client 0.25.0,
FastAPI 0.136.3, and a humming-kernels 0.1.17 overlay matching upstream.
Working directory: `/tmp/vllm-gauge-conflict-fix`.

```bash
export VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1
export PYTHONPATH=/tmp/vllm-gauge-conflict-test-deps:/tmp/vllm-gauge-conflict-fix
PYTHON=/home/billyae/vllm/.venv/bin/python

"$PYTHON" -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_metrics.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_metrics.py \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_metrics.py \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_metrics_reader.py \
  tests/v1/metrics/test_histogram_buckets.py -q

"$PYTHON" -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/rl/weight_transfer_metrics/test_weight_operation_metrics.py \
  tests/entrypoints/rl/state_transitions/test_sleep.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/instrumentator/test_metrics.py -m cpu_test -q

"$PYTHON" -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/exception_handling/test_http_status_metrics.py -q

env PATH=/home/billyae/vllm/.venv/bin:/snap/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin \
  "$PYTHON" -m pre_commit run --files $(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD)

env PATH=/home/billyae/.cache/pre-commit/repo47uoetiv/py_env-python3.12/bin:/home/billyae/vllm/.venv/bin:/usr/bin:/bin \
  "$PYTHON" tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12 $(git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD)
```

Pre-rebase compatibility checks prepended `/tmp/vllm-gauge-prometheus-018`, `-022`, or `-026`
to `PYTHONPATH` (the same `vllm-gauge-prometheus-` prefix for each). The base
environment supplies 0.25.0. The final startup/recreation selection was
`-k '(exported_before_first_stats and native) or survive_recorder_recreation'`;
the cleanup selection was `-k unregister_only_removes_vllm_defaults`.

The live harness used an editable GPU environment with official precompiled
artifacts. Its final native run launched the equivalent of:

```bash
env VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cuda PYTHONPATH=/tmp/vllm-gauge-late-logger-fix \
  VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=0 \
  VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 VLLM_LOG_STATS_INTERVAL=1 \
  /tmp/vllm-gauge-late-logger-runtime/.venv/bin/python \
  -m vllm.entrypoints.cli.main serve facebook/opt-125m \
  --revision 27dcfa74d334bc871f3234de431e71c6eeba5dd6 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 34981 --api-server-count 2 \
  --dtype float16 --max-model-len 512 --max-num-seqs 4 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 512 --enforce-eager --enable-prefix-caching \
  --enable-sleep-mode --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --block-size 16 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.15 --kv-cache-memory-bytes 67108864 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"OffloadingConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use":67108864}}'
```

Startup exposed all three native usage gauges at zero for both API PIDs and
all eight dev-operation labels at zero. Send the completion payload above,
reset the GPU prefix cache via `POST /reset_prefix_cache`, and resend it; the
native load counter reached 4718592 bytes. Then check level-1 sleep/wake and
level-0 keep/release-KV-cache/wake flows and compare the completion again.
Final in-flight counts were zero. The final harness result was:

```json
{
  "connector": "native",
  "api_workers": 2,
  "load_counter": 4718592.0,
  "completion_text": "m and I do not know if I",
  "status": "passed"
}
```

</details>

## Details

Mostrecent gauges omit unset timestamp-zero samples. Calling `.set(0)` to seed
them gives a late writer the newest timestamp and can replace real stats. A
private cached timestamp check is not atomic across gauge objects either.
Startup defaults now live in a lock-protected process-local dictionary; vLLM's
multiprocess collector adds only missing series. No initialization write touches
real mostrecent storage, and a real zero supersedes a fallback normally.

The instrumentator's exporter otherwise constructs a plain multiprocess
collector and bypasses the fallback-aware registry. Both metrics routes now use
vLLM's scrape registry, separate from HTTP instrumentation to avoid duplicates.
Defaults require this registry; an external plain collector does not see them.
Read-only private mode/storage-kind/bound-label metadata remains a compatibility
dependency. Cleanup removes only `vllm:` fallback entries.

Native usage gauges opt in via metadata. The rebase preserves upstream's
`multiprocess_mode="mostrecent"` alongside the optional startup value. Both
connectors now use scrape-time defaults for this mode, and the native late-writer
case is covered too. Explicit all/liveall modes retain their existing zero-on-bind
behavior without redundant initialization writes. Runtime observations still use
ordinary setters.
Development-operation singletons initialize during router registration, not
module import, after multiprocess storage selection. The startup test includes
upstream's new RL `shutdown` operation. No new dependency, scheduler
change, per-token work, or GPU synchronization is introduced.

AI assistance (Codex) was used for investigation, implementation, review, testing,
and preparation of this description.

- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

 @pytest.mark.cpu_test

     attach_metrics_router(app)
 
     with TestClient(app, raise_server_exceptions=False) as client:
+        startup = text_string_to_metric_families(client.get("/metrics").text)
+        assert {
+            sample.labels["operation"]: sample.value
+            for family in startup
+            for sample in family.samples
+            if sample.name == "vllm:sleep_mode_operations_in_flight"
+        } == {"sleep": 0, "release_kv_cache_memory": 0, "wake": 0}
         assert client.request(method, path).status_code == status
         response = client.get("/metrics")

@@ -154,36 +154,73 @@ def test_rejected_request_is_not_recorded(registry):
     assert sample(registry, DURATION, "update") is None
 
 
-def test_default_recorder_is_created_lazily_on_the_default_registry():
-    """The default recorder registers on the process registry only when first used.
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("multiprocess", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "feature,prefix,operations",
+    [
+        (
+            "rlhf",
+            "rl_weight_update",
+            ("init", "shutdown", "start", "start_draft", "update", "finish"),
+        ),
+        ("sleep", "sleep_mode", ("sleep", "release_kv_cache_memory", "wake")),
+    ],
+)
+def test_router_initializes_gauges_without_import_time_registration(
+    tmp_path, multiprocess, feature, prefix, operations
+):
+    """Router setup exports idle gauges without registering them at import time.
 
     Runs in a fresh interpreter: the registry is process-global, so a route test
     elsewhere in the session may already have registered these collectors, and
     "not registered yet" would then be unobservable.
     """
     probe = """
+import importlib
+import sys
 from prometheus_client import REGISTRY
+from fastapi import FastAPI
+from vllm.v1.metrics.prometheus import get_prometheus_registry
 
-from vllm.entrypoints.rl.online import metrics as rl_metrics
+feature, prefix = sys.argv[1:3]
+if feature == "rlhf":
+    module = "vllm.entrypoints.rl.online"
+    from vllm.entrypoints.rl.factories import register_rl_api_routers as attach_router
+else:
+    module = f"vllm.entrypoints.serve.dev.{feature}"
+    attach_router = importlib.import_module(f"{module}.api_router").attach_router
+metrics_module = importlib.import_module(f"{module}.metrics")
 
 NAMES = [
-    "vllm:rl_weight_update_operation_duration_seconds",
-    "vllm:rl_weight_update_operations_in_flight",
+    f"vllm:{prefix}_operation_duration_seconds",
+    f"vllm:{prefix}_operations_in_flight",
 ]
-assert rl_metrics._metrics is None

+class _MultiProcessCollectorWithInitialValues(multiprocess.MultiProcessCollector):
+    def collect(self) -> Iterable[Metric]:
+        with _initial_gauge_values_lock:
+            defaults = {
+                name: tuple(values.values())
+                for name, values in _initial_gauge_values.items()
+            }
+        for metric in super().collect():
+            initial_values = defaults.pop(metric.name, ())
+            if initial_values:
+                labels = {
+                    tuple(sorted(sample.labels.items())) for sample in metric.samples
+                }
+                for initial in initial_values:
+                    sample = initial.samples[0]
+                    if tuple(sorted(sample.labels.items())) not in labels:
+                        metric.samples.append(sample)
+            yield metric
+        for initial_values in defaults.values():
+            first = initial_values[0]
+            metric = GaugeMetricFamily(first.name, first.documentation, unit=first.unit)
+            metric.samples = [initial.samples[0] for initial in initial_values]
+            yield metric

+def set_gauge_initial_value(gauge: Gauge, value: float) -> None:
+    """Initialize a gauge without replacing real multiprocess mostrecent samples.
+
+    In multiprocess mostrecent modes, defaults are only exposed through
+    get_prometheus_registry(), not a plain MultiProcessCollector.
+    Multiprocess all/liveall gauges already expose zero on creation, so a
+    zero default leaves their storage unchanged.
+
+    Args:
+        gauge: An unlabeled gauge or a child with all labels bound.
+        value: Startup value.
+
+    """
+    storage = getattr(gauge, "_value", None)
+    mode = getattr(gauge, "_multiprocess_mode", None)
+    is_multiprocess = getattr(storage, "_multiprocess", False)
+    if is_multiprocess and mode in ("all", "liveall") and value == 0:
+        return
+    if is_multiprocess and mode in (
+        "mostrecent",
+        "livemostrecent",
+    ):
+        # Defaults belong in the scrape, not the mmap that real writers update.
+        for metric in gauge.collect():
+            for sample in metric.samples:
+                sample_labels = dict(zip(gauge._labelnames, gauge._labelvalues))
+                sample_labels.update(sample.labels)
+                initial = GaugeMetricFamily(
+                    metric.name,
+                    metric.documentation,
+                    labels=list(sample_labels),
+                    unit=metric.unit,
+                )
+                initial.add_metric(list(sample_labels.values()), float(value))
+                labels = tuple(sorted(sample_labels.items()))
+                with _initial_gauge_values_lock:
+                    _initial_gauge_values.setdefault(metric.name, {})[labels] = initial
+        return
